misconceptions.description: Treating every cell reference as relative, so a shared value like a tax rate shifts and breaks when the formula is copied down
misconceptions.trigger: learner copies a formula that reuses one fixed cell without locking it with dollar signs
misconceptions.feedback: Lock a reused value with an absolute reference such as $F$1 so it stays fixed when copied. Leave per-row inputs relative so they shift correctly.

misconceptions.description: Assuming AVERAGE treats blank cells as zeros, or dividing a SUM by a hard-coded row count that includes empty cells
misconceptions.trigger: learner divides a SUM by a fixed number instead of using AVERAGE on a range with blanks
misconceptions.feedback: AVERAGE skips truly blank cells and divides by the count of real values. Do not divide by a hard-coded count that treats blanks as zeros.

misconceptions.description: Using COUNT to answer a how-many-meet-this-condition question, so every value is counted regardless of the criterion
misconceptions.trigger: learner reaches for COUNT when the question asks for a conditional count
misconceptions.feedback: Use COUNTIF with a criterion such as ">500" to count only matching cells. COUNT counts all numbers, not just the ones that meet the condition.
